### Module 02 — Comorbidity Co-occurrence Heatmap

# Comorbidity Co-occurrence Heatmap

***
**Learning objectives**
- Build a binary comorbidity matrix from ICD-10 flags
- Compute pairwise co-occurrence, phi coefficients, and odds ratios
- Cluster comorbidities with hierarchical linkage and display with a clustered heatmap
- Identify clinically significant comorbidity pairs
- Build a network graph of comorbidity associations

**Estimated time:** 2 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `dplyr` / tibble, ggplot2, `stats`, igraph

## 1. Setup & Dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

# ── Dataset ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 800
sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers   <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                   N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
ages     <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
set.seed(99)

# Correlated comorbidity structure (realistic co-occurrence)
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)   # 3 latent factors
logistic <- function(x) plogis(x)

diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
hypertension  <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.7 * base[, 1] + 0.3 * base[, 2] - 0.2))
obesity       <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 1] + 0.4 * base[, 2] - 0.8))
ckd           <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 1] + 0.6 * diabetes - 1.2))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] + 0.5 * hypertension - 1.5))
afib          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.3 * base[, 2] + 0.4 * heart_failure - 1.8))
copd          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] - 1.0))
depression    <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.3 * base[, 3] + 0.2 * base[, 1] - 1.4))
anxiety       <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] + 0.4 * depression - 1.6))
sleep_apnea   <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * obesity + 0.3 * base[, 1] - 1.5))

df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  los_days      = los_days,
  diabetes      = diabetes,
  hypertension  = hypertension,
  obesity       = obesity,
  ckd           = ckd,
  heart_failure = heart_failure,
  afib          = afib,
  copd          = copd,
  depression    = depression,
  anxiety       = anxiety,
  sleep_apnea   = sleep_apnea,
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14)
)

COMORBS <- c("diabetes", "hypertension", "obesity", "ckd", "heart_failure",
             "afib", "copd", "depression", "anxiety", "sleep_apnea")

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
```

## 3. Phi Coefficient Matrix (Strength of Association)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
phi_coeff <- function(a, b) {
  # Phi coefficient for two binary variables.  Range: -1 to +1.
  ct <- table(a, b)
  if (!all(dim(ct) == c(2, 2))) return(0)
  n    <- sum(ct)
  chi2 <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(ct)$statistic)
  sgn  <- sign(ct[2, 2] * ct[1, 1] - ct[1, 2] * ct[2, 1])
  as.numeric(sqrt(unname(chi2) / n) * sgn)
}

phi_matrix  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(COMORBS), ncol = length(COMORBS),
                      dimnames = list(COMORBS, COMORBS))
pval_matrix <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(COMORBS), ncol = length(COMORBS),
                      dimnames = list(COMORBS, COMORBS))
for (c1 in COMORBS) {
  for (c2 in COMORBS) {
    phi_matrix[c1, c2] <- phi_coeff(df[[c1]], df[[c2]])
    if (c1 != c2) {
      pval_matrix[c1, c2] <- suppressWarnings(
        chisq.test(table(df[[c1]], df[[c2]]))$p.value
      )
    } else {
      pval_matrix[c1, c2] <- 1
    }
  }
}

cat("Top 10 comorbidity pairs by phi coefficient:\n")
```

## 4. Clustered Heatmap


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Hierarchical clustering on phi matrix
hc  <- hclust(dist(phi_matrix, method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
ord <- hc$order
phi_ord <- phi_matrix[ord, ord]
phi_heat <- as.data.frame(as.table(phi_ord), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(phi_heat) <- c("cond_1", "cond_2", "phi")
phi_heat$cond_1 <- factor(phi_heat$cond_1, levels = rownames(phi_ord))
phi_heat$cond_2 <- factor(phi_heat$cond_2, levels = colnames(phi_ord))

p_cl <- ggplot(phi_heat, aes(x = cond_1, y = cond_2, fill = phi)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", phi)), size = 2.8) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2563EB", mid = "white", high = "#DC2626",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.5, 0.5),
                       name = "Phi coefficient") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Comorbidity co-occurrence — phi coefficients (Ward clustering)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_health() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
print(p_cl)
```

## 5. Odds Ratios for Key Pairs


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
odds_ratio <- function(a, b) {
  # Odds ratio and 95% CI (Woolf method) for two binary variables.
  ct <- as.matrix(table(a, b))
  if (!all(dim(ct) == c(2, 2))) return(c(NA, NA, NA))
  # Apply 0.5 continuity correction if any cell is 0
  ct <- ct + 0.5
  OR <- (ct[2, 2] * ct[1, 1]) / (ct[1, 2] * ct[2, 1])
  log_or <- log(OR)
  se_log <- sqrt(1 / ct[1, 1] + 1 / ct[1, 2] + 1 / ct[2, 1] + 1 / ct[2, 2])
  lo <- exp(log_or - 1.96 * se_log)
  hi <- exp(log_or + 1.96 * se_log)
  round(c(OR, lo, hi), 2)
}

top_pairs <- phi_long %>%
  filter(significant) %>%
  arrange(desc(phi)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8)

or_df <- top_pairs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    or_ci = list(odds_ratio(df[[as.character(cond_1)]], df[[as.character(cond_2)]])),
    Pair  = paste(cond_1, "×", cond_2),
    Phi   = round(phi, 3),
    OR    = or_ci[1],
    lo    = or_ci[2],
    hi    = or_ci[3],
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%s–%s", lo, hi)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Pair, Phi, OR, `95% CI`, lo, hi)
cat("Odds ratios for top comorbidity pairs:\n")
```

## 6. Comorbidity Network Graph


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
threshold <- 0.15  # minimum phi to draw an edge
sig_pairs <- phi_long %>%
  filter(abs(phi) > threshold, significant)

vertices <- tibble(
  name = COMORBS,
  prev = map_dbl(COMORBS, ~ mean(df[[.x]]))
)

g <- graph_from_data_frame(sig_pairs %>% transmute(from = cond_1, to = cond_2, phi),
                           directed = FALSE, vertices = vertices)
E(g)$weight <- abs(E(g)$phi)
set.seed(42)
lay <- layout_with_fr(g)

e_col <- ifelse(E(g)$phi > 0, "#DC2626", "#2563EB")
v_size <- 8 + vertices$prev[match(V(g)$name, vertices$name)] * 40

op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0), bg = "white")
plot(
  g,
  layout              = lay,
  vertex.size         = v_size,
  vertex.color        = "#F0E6FF",
  vertex.frame.color  = "#6A4C93",
  vertex.label.cex    = 0.9,
  vertex.label.font   = 2,
  vertex.label.color  = "grey15",
  edge.width          = E(g)$weight * 8,
  edge.color          = e_col,
  main = "Comorbidity network (edge width ∝ phi coefficient, node size ∝ prevalence)"
)
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Positive association", "Negative association"),
       col = c("#DC2626", "#2563EB"), lwd = 3, bty = "n", cex = 0.9)
```

## 7. Knowledge Check
1. Why is the phi coefficient preferred over raw co-occurrence percentages for comparing comorbidity strength?
2. Diabetes and CKD cluster together. Name the clinical mechanism driving this.
3. An OR of 2.8 for obesity × sleep apnea means what, in plain language?
4. In the network graph, what would a negative phi edge (blue) between two conditions mean?
5. Re-run the clustermap restricted to patients aged 65+. Do the clusters change?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Exercise 5 — clustermap for 65+ patients
df_65 <- df %>% filter(age >= 65)
phi_65 <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(COMORBS), ncol = length(COMORBS),
                 dimnames = list(COMORBS, COMORBS))
for (c1 in COMORBS) {
  for (c2 in COMORBS) {
    phi_65[c1, c2] <- phi_coeff(df_65[[c1]], df_65[[c2]])
  }
}
hc65  <- hclust(dist(phi_65, method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
ord65 <- hc65$order
phi_65_ord <- phi_65[ord65, ord65]

names(heat65) <- c("cond_1", "cond_2", "phi")
heat65$cond_1 <- factor(heat65$cond_1, levels = rownames(phi_65_ord))

  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2563EB", mid = "white", high = "#DC2626",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-0.5, 0.5)) +
```
